subject: Clarify cross-region recovery scope for Greenwood integration
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@greenwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, procurement@greenwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2029 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on cross-region RTO/RPO responsibilities

Hi Olga and team,

Thanks for sending the updated SLA draft (attached). Before we circulate this to our legal and cloud ops, I need a few clarifications on the cross-region failover section so our architecture review has the right ask. High level: Greenwood will require a maximum RTO of 30 minutes for production inference traffic during a region outage, and an RPO no greater than 5 minutes for customer session state.

Specifically:
- Who is responsible for spinning up warm-standby capacity in the secondary region (Redwood or Greenwood)?
- Is there an automated failover policy (DNS vs. load balancer vs. application-level)? If DNS, what's the expected TTL and detection window we should budget for?
- If we use Redwood Private in our VPC, what evidence/logs/attestations can you provide to show the standby was available and ready prior to failover (for audit purposes)?

We also attached a shortlist of regulatory items that will need confirmation (SOC2 audit trails, retention of request logs for 1 year). Can you confirm which items you can provide as part of standard Private deployment and which will require a custom addendum?

Appreciate a concise matrix so we can mark items as accepted/needs-addendum.

Best,
Marta

--
Marta Lopez
Head of Cloud Architecture, Greenwood Financial
procurement@greenwood.com
Attachment: Greenwood_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@greenwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on cross-region RTO/RPO responsibilities

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. I summarized below and called out where we think a standard offering covers Greenwood vs. where an addendum is typical. Short answer: Redwood can meet the RTO/RPO targets with a warm-standby configuration but there are tradeoffs (reservation vs. burst) and audit evidence expectations to discuss.

Summary (high level):
- Warm-standby provisioning: Redwood can operate warm-standby as an optional managed responsibility (reserved capacity in secondary region) or provide runbooks + automation for Greenwood to operate in their VPC. Standard Private without reserved capacity uses a cold/burst model which may not meet 30m RTO for large sustained traffic.
- Failover mechanism: we support application-level health checks + regional routing via our smart routing plane. For Private VPC installs we'll typically use a VIP/Load-Balancer handoff + upstream DNS failover; TTL recommendations: 60s for critical endpoints, but DNS propagation behavior depends on customer infra.
- Audit evidence: For Redwood Private we can provide time-stamped activation logs, cluster readiness metrics, and an attestation PDF from our ops team. SOC2 artifacts require an NDA and scoped request; full audit packages are treated as a professional service.

I'd like to propose a short matrix and two options you can choose from:
A) Managed warm-standby (Redwood reserves capacity in secondary region) — meets 30m RTO, includes activation logs and quarterly readiness tests (add-on fee).
B) Self-managed warm-standby (Greenwood owns capacity) — Redwood provides automation templates, runbooks, and support onboarding; RTO depends on Greenwood's capacity provisioning.

I'll loop in Markus and Laura to confirm cost/contract implications and the exact artifacts we can commit to in an addendum. If Greenwood can take option A we can commit to the RTO/RPO and include explicit log retention terms.

Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@greenwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2029 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on cross-region RTO/RPO responsibilities

Marta — quick notes from an operational and contracting lens:
- Option A (managed warm-standby): we will need a reserved capacity commitment (monthly minimum) for the secondary region. That commitment defines activation latency guarantees.
- Option B (self-managed): we can provide automation and a playbook, but we must carve out the guaranteed RTO in the SLA and instead offer an onboarding milestone schedule.

Regarding audit artifacts: we can commit to providing activation/event logs and a signed quarterly attestation for readiness checks as an SLA attachment. Full SOC2 packages (control descriptions, audit reports) would be shared under an executed NDA and usually via a compliance portal (we send temporary access).

Laura — can you draft a short addendum bullet list we can present to Greenwood that enumerates the deliverables for Option A vs Option B? I started a cost stub but we should avoid hard numbers until procurement signals preference.

Thanks,
Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@greenwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 Mar 2029 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on cross-region RTO/RPO responsibilities

Hi Marta — attached is a proposed Responsibility Matrix and a short addendum draft that maps each audit artifact and the retention term. Highlights:
- For managed warm-standby (Option A) we commit to: 30m RTO, 5m RPO for session state assuming KV caching is enabled, activation logs retained for 12 months, quarterly readiness tests (results shared), and a signed attestation after each test.
- For self-managed (Option B) we commit to providing automation templates + 30-day onboarding runbook; RTO is best-effort outside the reserved-capacity contract.

I've attached the workbook with the responsibility mapping and a sample attestation language so Greenwood can pass it to compliance. If Greenwood wants the SOC2 bundle we'll require the mutual NDA; I included a link to our compliance intake form in the doc.

Attachment: redwood-recovery-responsibility-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Please review and tell us which option you prefer; if Option A, we'll prepare an addendum and a one-page pricing summary.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@greenwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 Mar 2029 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on cross-region RTO/RPO responsibilities

Laura/Markus/Olga — thank you, that matrix is exactly what our compliance team needed. Greenwood prefers Option A (managed warm-standby) to avoid runbook operational risk. Next steps:
1) Send the addendum + one-page pricing summary so procurement can review.
2) We'll prepare an NDA for SOC2 access; procurement@greenwood.com will send the document later today.
3) Can Redwood confirm target cadence for the first readiness test after contract signature? Greenwood requests within 30 days post-signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Marta

--
Marta Lopez
Head of Cloud Architecture, Greenwood Financial
